steps.say: A magnet pulls, or attracts, things made of iron or steel. These are magnetic materials.

figure.alt: A magnet next to a paperclip and a nail.

steps.say: Most materials are not magnetic. Even many metals, like aluminium and copper, are not magnetic.
Every magnet has two poles: north (N) and south (S). The force is strongest at the poles.
Opposite poles attract. Like poles repel.
steps.show: N and S attract. N and N repel. S and S repel.

steps.say: Magnetic force can act through paper, plastic and water. The magnet does not have to touch.
A compass needle is a small magnet. It lines up with the Earth's magnetism and points north.

options.why: Aluminium is a metal that is not magnetic.

hints: Only a few materials are magnetic.
Think about what nails are made of.
Which one is a metal used to make steel?
check.explanation: Iron is magnetic. Steel, which is made from iron, is magnetic too.

check.prompt: A north pole and a south pole will ___ each other.
hints: Different poles do not push apart.
The science word starts with a.
check.explanation: Opposite poles attract, so north and south pull together.
